name: Torrontés

lines.s10: Torrontés is Argentina's own white, scented like a rose garden with peach and orange blossom, yet dry and fresh when you taste it.
lines.s20: Torrontés grows high in the Andes of north west Argentina, above all around the town of Cafayate in Salta. Its scent of rose petal, jasmine and ripe peach promises sweetness, and then it drinks dry and fresh, with a faint bitter twist at the end.
lines.s45: Torrontés plays one trick: it smells sweet and drinks dry. It is Argentina's own white grape, at home around Cafayate in the far north west, where vines stand over a mile high in desert sun. The scent is rose petal, jasmine and ripe peach. The taste is dry, light and fresh, with a faint bitter twist. Oak would smother that perfume, so the wine is made in cool steel tanks and bottled young. Pour it with empanadas, ceviche or anything with a little chilli heat. It arose by chance in Argentina, a cross of Muscat of Alexandria and the mission grape the Spanish brought.
lines.sale: Torrontés gives you all the perfume of a sweet wine, rose petal and ripe peach, and then finishes clean and dry. I would pour it tonight beside the crawfish étouffée, where the scent meets the cayenne and the freshness cuts the butter.

glass.lead: Rose petal, jasmine and orange blossom over white peach and lemon, dry and light, with a faint bitter note on the finish.

ladder.where: The upper Calchaquí valleys, higher and colder than Cafayate
Cafayate in Salta, La Rioja's Famatina Valley, San Juan and Mendoza

glass.structure: Dry, though the scent suggests sweetness. Acidity medium to medium plus, alcohol medium to medium plus, body light to medium, with a faint bitterness on the finish.

home.home: Argentina, where it was born. Cafayate in Salta, about 1,700 metres up in the Calchaquí valleys, is the address a guest meets, with La Rioja, San Juan and Mendoza behind it. Vines are often trained on a high pergola that shades the fruit, and the wine is fermented cool in steel, dry, and bottled young.
home.abroad: It hardly travels: Chile and Uruguay grow a little, and much of Chile's goes to the still for pisco. The Torrontés of Galicia in Spain is a different, unrelated grape that shares the name.

service.temp: 45 to 50 degrees Fahrenheit, 7 to 10 degrees Celsius: well chilled, so the perfume stays fresh.
service.glass: A white wine glass, with room above the wine for the perfume to gather.
service.decant: No. A light aromatic white wants only a cold bottle and a clean glass.
service.age: The freshest bottle you can find, within a year or two of the harvest; the perfume fades.

with.why: the match of its own home in Salta
lime and chilli meet its lemon and freshness
perfume and freshness against cayenne and butter
a rose scented, dry white sits easily beside chilli heat

labels.means: The town in Salta's Calchaquí valleys, about 1,700 metres up: the address a list most often names for Torrontés.
The full name of the most perfumed of three Torrontés varieties, after La Rioja province; labels usually say only Torrontés.
Late harvest: a sweet Torrontés, where nearly every other still bottle is dry.
The high valley system shared by Salta, Tucumán and Catamarca; Cafayate lies at the southern end of Salta's stretch.

guest.q: It smells so sweet. Is this a sweet wine?
guest.a: No. The perfume comes from its Muscat parent, but the wine is fermented dry. A bottle marked cosecha tardía, late harvest, is the sweet one.

guest.q: Is this the same Torrontés I drank in Spain?
guest.a: No. Galicia grows a grape of the same name that is no relation. Argentina's Torrontés arose in Argentina, a cross of Muscat of Alexandria and the mission grape, Criolla Chica.

guest.q: Why does the label print the altitude?
guest.a: Because the height is the point. Around Cafayate the vines stand about 1,700 metres up, where strong sun ripens the fruit and cold nights keep the wine fresh.

guest.q: Should I keep a bottle for a few years?
guest.a: I would not. Its charm is the fresh perfume, and that fades in the bottle. Drink it cold, within a year or two of the vintage.

compare.tell: Muscat Blanc is grapier and softer in acidity, often sweet or lightly sparkling; Torrontés carries the same rose and orange blossom on a dry, fresher frame with a bitter finish.
Gewürztraminer is oilier, fuller and lower in acidity, with lychee and ginger; Torrontés shares the rose petal but is lighter and fresher, with a bitter finish.
Viognier is fuller and richer, with apricot and honeysuckle and soft acidity; Torrontés is lighter, with rose petal where Viognier has apricot.

cards.front: Torrontés: which country is home, and which town does a list name?
cards.back: Argentina. Cafayate, in Salta's Calchaquí valleys, about 1,700 metres up, is the address a list most often names; La Rioja, San Juan and Mendoza grow it too.

cards.front: Which two grapes are the parents of Torrontés Riojano?
cards.back: Muscat of Alexandria and Criolla Chica, the mission grape also called Listán Prieto: a natural cross that arose in Argentina. The Muscat parent explains the perfume.

cards.front: Torrontés blind: what parts it from Muscat and from Gewürztraminer?
cards.back: It smells as sweetly of rose petal and jasmine as either, then drinks dry, with fresher acidity, a lighter body and a faint bitter finish. Gewürztraminer is oilier, with lychee; Muscat is grapier and softer.

questions.q: A blind white is pale lemon with green tints. The nose is all rose petal, jasmine and ripe peach and seems to promise sugar, yet the palate is dry, light and fresh, with a faint bitter finish. Which grape and origin fit it?
questions.exp: Rose petal and jasmine that promise sugar, on a dry, light, fresh palate with a bitter twist, mark Torrontés. Gewürztraminer from Alsace would be oilier and fuller, with lychee and lower acidity.

questions.q: A guest sniffs her glass of Torrontés, says it smells like dessert, and asks why a dry wine should smell so sweet. What is the reason?
opts: One of its parents is Muscat of Alexandria
Unfermented sugar is left in the wine
It is aged in new oak barrels
It is fortified with grape spirit
questions.exp: Torrontés Riojano is a natural cross of Muscat of Alexandria and Criolla Chica, and the Muscat parent gives the perfume. The wine is fermented dry, so no sugar is left to explain it.

questions.q: A guest enjoys a Torrontés from Cafayate and asks whether to lay a case down for five years. What do you advise?
opts: Drink it young, within a year or two
Keep it five years to gain honey
Keep it ten years, as you would Riesling
Wait three years for the oak to settle
questions.exp: The charm of Torrontés is its fresh perfume, which fades in bottle, so it is drunk within a year or two. It is made in steel without oak, and it does not gain with age as Riesling can.

report: Mode home, as the plan fixes it: the grape's home is the New World, Argentina, and no Old World style of it reaches a list.
The say line is the Court's own respelling, tor-ron-TES, unchanged.

No Codex record is contradicted. The profile, the dials, the grid read and the region records for Salta, La Rioja, San Juan and Argentina supplied the fruit and flowers, the dry palate under a sweet nose, the bitter finish, the parentage (Muscat of Alexandria and Criolla Chica), the three Torrontés varieties, the pergola, the cool ferment in steel, Cafayate at about 1,700 metres, cosecha tardía and the unrelated Torrontés of Galicia.

The ladder: the Court's grid reads Salta and Mendoza as warm, so Cafayate sits on the warm rung. The moderate rung (the upper Calchaquí valleys, higher and colder than Cafayate: lime, lemon zest, jasmine) is a taster's reading of what more altitude does; the Codex says only that growers go up the valley for colder nights.

Abroad: small plantings in Chile and Uruguay, and Chile's going largely to pisco, rest on the standard reference works and on general references read through search; which of the three Torrontés varieties Chile grows is disputed among them, so the entry does not say.
Muscat grape and lychee are filed under tropical fruit for want of a nearer family; the reviewed profile says table grape and the grid read lychee.
The reviewed profile's other line uses the word phenolic; the entry says a faint bitter finish, as the brief asks of a spoken line.
Crawfish étouffée is the one dish from the Creole table. Empanadas, ceviche and chilli heat follow the Court's own sell line.
The sources were read through search results; this session could not open the hosts directly (argentina.gob.ar and the Wines of Argentina hosts are outside the session's network allowance).

checked.verdict: Sound after nine fixes. The parentage, the three varieties, the unrelated vine of Galicia, the pergola and the pisco of Chile were confirmed; two absolutes about sweetness, one of geography and one tell were wrong or loose.
changed: labels, Cosecha tardía: Late harvest: a sweet Torrontés, and the one style of it that is not dry now reads Late harvest: a sweet Torrontés, where nearly every other still bottle is dry. Argentina also bottles sparkling Torrontés, some of it sweet, and a few off dry and dessert wines, so late harvest is not the one style that is not dry.
guest[0].a: Only a bottle marked cosecha tardía, late harvest, is sweet now reads A bottle marked cosecha tardía, late harvest, is the sweet one. The same absolute, said to a guest.

labels, Valles Calchaquíes: Cafayate lies at its southern end now reads Cafayate lies at the southern end of Salta's stretch. The line itself says the valleys are shared with Tucumán and Catamarca, which lie south of Cafayate; the Codex Salta record runs the valleys down to Cafayate and then on into both.

labels, Torrontés Riojano: the perfumed one of three Torrontés varieties now reads the most perfumed of three Torrontés varieties. Sanjuanino is scented too, only less so; Mendocino is the least aromatic. A measured comparison, not a selling word.

compare, the Gewürztraminer tell: Torrontés is lighter and fresher, with rose petal and peach now reads Torrontés shares the rose petal but is lighter and fresher, with a bitter finish. Rose petal is Gewürztraminer too, as its own entry says, so it cannot part the two. Weight, freshness and the bitter finish do.

compare, the Muscat Blanc tell: Torrontés carries the same flowers on a dry, fresher frame now reads Torrontés carries the same rose and orange blossom on a dry, fresher frame. Flowers is a family word in disguise; the flowers are named.
food.with, Thai green curry: a floral, dry white sits easily beside chilli heat now reads a rose scented, dry white sits easily beside chilli heat. The family word floral, named.
lines.s45: the wine is made in cold steel and bottled young now reads the wine is made in cool steel tanks and bottled young. Cold steel is a blade to the ear; said aloud, the tank is clearer.

notIn: [] now reads ["treixadura"]. A question answered by Treixadura that lists Torrontes among Ribeiro's blending grapes is about the Galician vine, which the entry itself calls unrelated; without the phrase it joins this grape's drill by name. The gate pins only that the pool of each of the twenty is not empty.
open: Muscat grape is filed under tropical fruit beside lychee for want of a family that holds it, as the author reported. The Muscat Blanc entry files fresh table grape under orchard fruit, and the Court grid gives this grape no orchard fruit at all, so neither home is right; it stays where the author put it.
The Viognier tell gives apricot to Viognier and rose petal to Torrontés while this entry lists apricot among its own notes. It is the reviewed profile own confuse line, so it stays.
Which of the three Torrontés varieties Chile grows is disputed among the sources, and the entry does not say.
